Thanks Alex — great questions. Quick answers below and a couple of options to discuss in the deep-dive: 

1) Connectivity model: we support both models:
   - VPC peering / PrivateLink: preferred for managed deployments in AWS where you want no public internet egress; traffic remains within the backbone to Redwood endpoints in the chosen region.
   - Outbound-only via a pinned proxy: if your security policy allows strictly controlled outbound connections to a small set of endpoints (we can publish a short IP/FQDN list), that also works for health/metrics/license checks.
   - Air-gapped/on-prem: we provide an offline bundle (container images and install scripts) plus a local registry you host; no external outbound required after initial image transfer.

2) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys. Two common patterns: 
   - Use your cloud KMS (AWS KMS with CMKs) where Redwood's control plane does not have the plaintext keys; we encrypt data in the customer VPC.
   - For higher assurance, our private offering can be configured to work with customer HSMs (either via a secure connector or by running key operations entirely within your environment). We will have Marissa (our security lead) join the tech deep-dive to walk through options and provide the specific architecture notes.

3) Image registry: yes — for the air-gapped option you'll host an internal registry. We provide signed images and a verification process, plus an upgrade path.

I'll attach a short SOC2 doc checklist (rdoc-soc2-request.xlsx) that procurement often asks for; filling that out will speed the procurement review.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive: 
- Wed, Mar 10 at 10:00 CET (preferred)
- Thu, Mar 11 at 14:00 CET
